memory_candidates.content: To verify a downstream artifact carries a drafted quote byte-for-byte rather than a paraphrase, extract the same delimiter-bounded block from both files with `sed -n '/start-pattern/,/end-pattern/p'` and diff the two extractions directly, rather than eyeballing the text -- a mechanical check catches a single dropped em-dash or reflowed line that a read-through would miss.

sapience_notes.subject: Durability of a gitignored specs/ (task-state) tree
sapience_notes.value: Recommend documenting the exposure rather than building a recovery mechanism: every real recovery option (a sibling repository, or a periodic orphan-branch archive commit in the same repository) recovers bytes only by giving the tree a second place to live, and that second place is itself a branch/remote/repo that every branch- or repo-enumerating surface (git fetch --all, git branch -a, CI sweeps) must learn to skip -- reintroducing the exact cross-branch/cross-repo churn an ignored posture exists to remove.

sapience_notes.subject: Existing backup-adjacent patterns in this codebase
sapience_notes.value: No mechanism anywhere in this codebase backs up a gitignored specs/-style task-state tree today. The two nearest analogues -- a pre-wipe local snapshot copy of settings files before a full config regeneration, and a global curated-reference sibling repository used for literature management -- both fail to transfer: neither matches a write pattern of many small mutations per task-dispatch, sustained for the life of the repository.

sapience_notes.subject: External host-level file-sync/snapshot as a durability option
sapience_notes.value: An external, host-level sync or snapshot tool is the one durability option that doesn't touch git and so avoids cross-branch churn, but it fails on a different ground: whether it is actually configured and covering the relevant path is unverifiable from inside the repository, and adopting one is not a decision the repository's own tooling can make. It collapses into 'document the exposure, tell the reader to check their own host' -- i.e. the same outcome as building nothing.

sapience_notes.subject: Orphan-branch archive commits as a durability mechanism
sapience_notes.value: A periodic archive commit onto an orphan branch in the same repository still participates in every branch-enumerating git surface (git branch -a, git fetch/push --all, CI branch-protection sweeps, stale-branch cleanup tools), so it reintroduces the same class of cross-branch churn a tracked/visible specs/ posture was criticized for -- just relocated to a branch that never appears in a pull request instead of removed.

sapience_notes.subject: Drafting a statement for a downstream record to place verbatim
sapience_notes.value: When a research or planning artifact drafts text for a different, later record to insert unmodified (e.g. a durability-exposure statement for a documentation task to place), writing it in the negative framing ('no mechanism preserves X' rather than a descriptive feature list) measurably reduces the risk that a future reader skims it as evidence a protection already exists.
